episodes.180669: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over Middle Tennessee on July 13, 2023 and into the early morning hours of July 14th. One of these thunderstorms in southeast Wilson County produced locally heavy rainfall, causing minor flooding in the Watertown area. Elsewhere, a lightning strike struck a gas line in west Brentwood.
episodes.180674: Widely scattered showers and storms developed ahead of a cold front as it approached central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of July 13, 2023. The storms produced sporadic wind damage and one report of quarter-sized hail.
episodes.180675: Widely scattered storms developed in a warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of July 14, 2023, with a weak stationary frontal boundary draped across the area. One storm in particular was able to sustain itself from Centre County east-northeastward and across southern Clinton County and Lycoming County, producing sporadic wind damage and sub-severe (penny-sized) hail along the way.
episodes.180687: Severe thunderstorms developed across most counties in the Nebraska Panhandle 13 July 2023.
episodes.180700: Severe storms tracked southeast across Converse and Platte Counties on 14 July.
episodes.180747: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts in Brevard and Martin Counties.
episodes.180755: During the afternoon of July 14, 2023 a strong storm formed in northeast Kansas and eventually transformed into a strong squall line that impacted far eastern Kansas and western Missouri. This storm left a swath of wind damage mainly through the heart of the Kansas City metro area in the form of widespread tree damage. Several structures were impacted by falling trees as the storm moved through the city, and into central Missouri. The highest reported wind gust came from western Johnson County where a personal weather station recorded 89 mph wind just west of Lenexa. Numerous wind reports, both estimated and measured were over 70 mph. At one point nearly 200,000 people across the Kansas City metro lost power. As of the next day, roughly 60,000 Kansas Citians were still without power.
episodes.180756: During the afternoon of July 14, 2023 a strong storm formed in northeast Kansas and eventually transformed into a strong squall line that impacted far eastern Kansas and western Missouri. This storm left a swath of wind damage mainly through the heart of the Kansas City metro area in the form of widespread tree damage. Several structures were impacted by falling trees as the storm moved through the city, and into central Missouri. The highest reported wind gust came from western Johnson County where a personal weather station recorded 89 mph wind just west of Lenexa. Numerous wind reports, both estimated and measured were over 70 mph. At one point nearly 200,000 people across the Kansas City metro lost power. As of the next day, roughly 60,000 Kansas Citians were still without power.
episodes.180758: Higher low-level moisture on July 13th and a backdoor cold front replenishing this moisture for July 14th and 15th combined with robust upper level wind shear produced three days of severe weather across eastern NM. Severe weather impacts were limited to northeastern NM on the 13th and 14th, becoming more widespread across northeastern and east-central NM on the 15th. There were a few thunderstorm wind gusts measured in the vicinity of the White Sands Missile Range on the 13th and 14th, likely from dry microbursts as the exception for the 13th and 14th. More substantial reports of damage and large hail occurred on the 15th ranging from broken skylights, flooding, accumulated hail, and a tornado. Thankfully, there were no reports of injuries or casualties.
episodes.180822: Heavy rain from thunderstorms led to an isolated instance of flash flooding in Fairfax County.
episodes.180823: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to northern New Jersey from the late afternoon into the evening of July 14.  Rainfall totals were as high as 3 to around 7 inches.
episodes.180824: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to the Lehigh Valley and the Pocono Region of eastern Pennsylvania from the late afternoon into the evening of July 14.  Rainfall totals were as high as 3 to around 6 inches.
episodes.181192: A few thunderstorms developed during the evening hours over northeast Montana, with a couple reaching severe levels.
episodes.181220: Showers and thunderstorms developed in West Virginia on the afternoons of July 13th through 15th in the midst of weak disturbances passing through the area.  Strong wind gusts accompanying storms resulted in multiple downed trees across the state. Flash flooding also blocked sections of a road in Raleigh County on the 13th while another isolated instance of flash flooding occurred on the 15th in Clay County. Storms tapered down with the loss of daytime heating after sunset each evening.
episodes.181370: A weak mid level short wave trough combined with very hot temperatures to generate scattered thunderstorms late on the afternoon of the 13th. The hot temperatures allowed for a deeply mixed boundary layer giving thunderstorms high cloud bases. These storms slowly moved to the east through the evening creating scattered severe wind gusts. A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Hackberry (Cottle County) measured a severe wind gust with outflow winds well away from the thunderstorm activity.
episodes.181426: An isolated severe thunderstorm quickly formed over northwest Kentucky in the heat of the afternoon. The storm pulsed up to severe levels for a brief time, with damaging winds downing trees on houses. The storm formed ahead of a cold front that trailed southwest across central Missouri from a low pressure center over the Great Lakes.
episodes.181538: Daytime heating helped the environment become unstable enough for isolated severe thunderstorms in portions of Northeastern Pennsylvania. There were a few reports of trees that were knocked down by the strong wind gusts.
episodes.181705: Intense and back-building thunderstorms led to severe weather and flash flooding across portions of the area.
episodes.181877: A cold front slowed as it approached the Appalachian Mountains, intersecting a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, several of which became severe producing widely scattered instances of wind damage and isolated large hail. A couple of localized considerable instances of wind damage were noted near Washington, DC, and its western suburbs.
episodes.181881: A cold front slowed as it approached the Appalachian Mountains, intersecting a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, several of which became severe producing widely scattered instances of wind damage and isolated large hail. A couple of localized considerable instances of wind damage were noted near Washington, DC, and its western suburbs.
episodes.181884: A cold front slowed as it approached the Appalachian Mountains, intersecting a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, several of which became severe producing widely scattered instances of wind damage and isolated large hail. A couple of localized considerable instances of wind damage were noted near Washington, DC, and its western suburbs.
episodes.181885: A cold front slowed as it approached the Appalachian Mountains, intersecting a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, several of which became severe producing widely scattered instances of wind damage and isolated large hail. A couple of localized considerable instances of wind damage were noted near Washington, DC, and its western suburbs.
episodes.181939: A cold front slowed as it approached the Appalachian Mountains, intersecting a hot, humid, and unstable airmass. This resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, several of which produced gale- to storm-force winds near the area waterways.
episodes.181987: Low pressure was moving across the St. Lawrence River area and southern New England was in a warm and humid airmass.  A line of strong thunderstorms formed in eastern New York and moved into western Massachusetts during the late evening.  Because of steepening mid-level lapse rates, the storms maintained intensity as they progressed into central and even portions of eastern Massachusetts.
episodes.181990: A cluster of thunderstorms moved northward into Connecticut during the morning ahead of a short-wave trough southwest of southern New England.  The showers and thunderstorms spread northeastward into the early afternoon.  One storm produced a lightning strike that started a house fire in northeast Massachusetts. Several roads were flooded in Worcester County.
episodes.182092: An upper level wave moved across northern and eastern Iowa. By peak afternoon heating, thunderstorms began developing along the boundary in northeast Iowa into southern Minnesota.  DCAPE approached 900 J/kg, supporting gusty winds with storms that developed. At the same time, deep layer shear over 40 knots and steep lapse rates supported hail growth, with several reports of quarter sized hail as the storms moved southeast.
episodes.182103: A hot and humid airmass was in place across central Illinois as a cold front approached from the northwest. Several thunderstorm clusters developed over the course of the evening, and these produced scattered wind damage and one instance of severe hail.
episodes.182170: Despite an upper ridge extending from the Desert Southwest into the Southern Plains, scattered diurnal storms developed during the evening of the 13th. While weak magnitudes of organizing wind shear existed across the area, storm organization occurred along the composite outflow from initial storms across western-north Texas into southwestern Oklahoma. Damaging downburst wind events and a few reports of large hail were received with the strongest storms.
episodes.182172: A long-track mesoscale convective system (MCS) tracked from southern Nebraska into the Ozarks during daytime hours on the 14th. The southwestern portion of this system clipped the far northeast forecast area (Kay County) and produced a report of wind damage near Ponca City. Further west, scattered supercell thunderstorms developed by the evening hours and produced reports of large hail near the community of Woodward.
episodes.182269: A broad upper trough was centered over Canada and extended southward over the Central Plains to the East Coast. Upper level disturbances had moved over the Central Plains at the base of the trough and provided lift. One of the upper disturbances moved over south central Nebraska in the late morning to early afternoon hours. CAPE was fairly high across the area and zero to six km wind shear was generally between 30 to 45 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally between 7 to 8 degrees C/km. ||Showers and thunderstorms developed across Nebraska during the morning hours. A cluster of storms moved into south central Nebraska from the west. One storm produced penny sized hail in Dawson County just after 10 AM CDT. Another storm strengthened as it moved in from the west and impacted Furnas County. This storm began by producing nickel sized hail at 10:40 AM CDT and ended by producing quarter size hail at 11:18 AM CDT. This storm had also produced a wind gust up to 64 mph.
episodes.182270: A broad upper trough was centered over Canada and extended southward over the Central Plains to the East Coast. Upper level disturbances had moved over the Central Plains at the base of the trough and provided lift. One of the upper disturbances moved over north central Kansas in the late morning to early afternoon hours. CAPE was fairly high across the area and zero to six km wind shear was generally between 30 to 45 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally between 7 to 8 degrees C/km.||Storms developed across northern Kansas during the late morning hours of July 14th. Storms were also moving southward into Kansas from Nebraska. A storm had moved southward from Nebraska into Phillips County in Kansas and produced golf ball size hail at 11:45 AM CDT. This storm also produced a wind gust of 75 mph in Phillips County that resulted in tree damage and continued southeastward to produce nickel size hail in Rooks County. Finally, the storm produced wind gusts estimated near 60 mph in Osborne County at 12:40 PM CDT that resulted in tree damage.
episodes.182461: Slow moving frontal boundary, combined with a weak upper level storm system and a moisture laden airmass contributed to the development of widely scattered afternoon thunderstorms. A couple of these storms became severe and produced damaging winds.
episodes.182513: Scattered thunderstorms, some with torrential rainfall affected portions of Addison and Rutland Counties. One to locally four inches of rain fell in a some areas, leading to a few reports of flash flooding and road washouts.
episodes.182619: A cold front passed through Northeastern Pennsylvania, triggering scattered showers and thunderstorms. An unstable environment supported multiple severe thunderstorms that contained damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.182881: An outbreak of multicell clusters and supercells developed across Southeast Michigan on the afternoon of July 14, 2023. These storms produced areas of wind damage, large hail to golf ball size, heavy rain, and an EF0 tornado in Sanilac County before moving eastward into Canada and the lakes during the evening. Numerous trees were downed across the region, and in the Thumb there were several reports of destroyed corn and wheat fields as well as several homes with damage to siding due to wind-blown hail.
episodes.182919: An isolated thunderstorm brought severe wind gusts in excess of 60 mph to southern Hyde and central Buffalo Counties during the mid-afternoon hours.
episodes.182981: A thunderstorm moving into southern Lake Huron produced a wind gust in excess of 40 knots.
episodes.182998: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.  In addition, weak steering flow resulted in some slow moving storms with reports of flash flooding, particularly in Jackson and Walton counties.
episodes.183037: A few surface boundaries, from upstream thunderstorms over Virginia and the North Carolina Foothills during the afternoon and evening on the 13th of July, converged upon and focused thunderstorm development over central North Carolina, as they settled generally southward throughout the morning through evening hours on the 14th. Damaging wind gusts and flash flooding resulted from a combination of slow-moving showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.183112: Several clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved southeast across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 14th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind in Sequoyah County.||Additional thunderstorms intensified and became well-organized over Kansas during the day as they moved southeast across the state. These thunderstorms formed a nearly solid line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved across eastern Oklahoma during the evening. The strongest storms produced damaging wind.
episodes.183113: Several clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved southeast across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 14th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind, a brief tornado, and flash flooding in Sebastian County.||Additional thunderstorms intensified and became well-organized over Kansas during the day as they moved southeast across the state. These thunderstorms formed a nearly solid line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved across northwestern Arkansas during the evening. The strongest storms produced damaging wind.
episodes.183288: Two groups of supercells moved out of South Dakota and into northern Nebraska during the afternoon and early evening, with the second eventually converging into a small squall line. Another cluster of supercells moved from the panhandle into southwest Nebraska and also evolved into a squall line. Several reports of large hail and damaging winds were received, primarily in Cherry County and a swath from Garden to Lincoln counties.
episodes.183289: Clusters of severe storms, some supercellular, traversed southwest Nebraska during the mid morning hours of July 14, resulting in multiple large hail reports.
episodes.183313: Thunderstorms developed across the Florida panhandle and produced very heavy rain that caused flooding.
episodes.183340: Scattered strong to severe storms during the afternoon and evening of July 14th impacted the Northern Plains into the Upper Mississippi River Valley. The primary threat was hail with penny sized reported near Stacyville (Mitchell County) and quarter sized hail reported near New Hampton (Fayette County).
episodes.183356: A slowly southward-moving front was draped across central Ohio and Pennsylvania on July 13th.  Warm air aloft initially kept storm development muted, but a mesoscaled convective vortex fired thunderstorms by early to mid-afternoon over the Middle Ohio Valley.  These storms lifted northeastward into an environment characterized by 40 to 50 knots of deep-layer shear and up to 2500 J/kg of mixed layer CAPE.  Dry air aloft also enhanced the downburst wind threat.  As a result, many reports of tree damage were received across southwest Pennsylvania, along with several instances of marginally severe hail.
episodes.183405: A cold front moving to the southeast across the Northland led to the development of sub-severe storms across the region. One storm across Bayfield County was able to produce hail to the size of nickels, but most of the storms only produced pea-sized hail.
episodes.183409: On the morning of July 14th, a cold front passed through Southwestern Nebraska allowing for thunderstorms to move through the region. One of these thunderstorms became severe and produced wind gusts up to 60 mph along with penny sized hail.
episodes.183410: On the morning of July 14th, a cold front passed through Northwestern Kansas allowing for thunderstorms to move through the region. One of these thunderstorms became severe and produced wind gusts up to 70 mph along with quarter sized hail.
episodes.183414: A moist and unstable airmass was present over southwest Alabama during the morning hours with PWATs near 2.5 inches. Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours over Sumter County.  Significant flooding occurred with radar estimated rainfall amounts of 6 to 8 inches fell over a three hour period. Additional storms developed on July 14th and produced localized flooding in Shelby County.
episodes.183424: A couple of isolated severe storms moved across the southern Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon/early evening hours of the 13th. One of which produced hail 1.25 in diameter. As the evening progressed these storms moved west to east merging with a line of storms from the Texas Panhandle and ran south through much of West Texas. Also a couple of initial supercells entered the northwestern combined Panhandles producing hail up to 1.25 in diameter as well. A complex eventually formed in southeast Colorado and moved southeast into the combined Panhandles becoming the main focus for severe storms going into the early AM hours of the 14th. Severe wind gusts became the main threat with winds reaching up to 75 mph measured, and 85 mph estimated from wind damage.
episodes.183425: A couple of isolated severe storms moved across the southern Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon/early evening hours of the 13th. One of which produced hail 1.25 in diameter. As the evening progressed these storms moved west to east merging with a line of storms from the Texas Panhandle and ran south through much of West Texas. Also a couple of initial supercells entered the northwestern combined Panhandles producing hail up to 1.25 in diameter as well. A complex eventually formed in southeast Colorado and moved southeast into the combined Panhandles becoming the main focus for severe storms going into the early AM hours of the 14th. Severe wind gusts became the main threat with winds reaching up to 75 mph measured, and 85 mph estimated from wind damage.
episodes.183438: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires and a few reports of flooding across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023. One injury was reported as a tree fell onto an occupied vehicle. Thousands were left without power across the Capital Region.||Additional isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening and early overnight hours on July 14-15, 2023 producing additional reports of hail, wind damage and flooding.
episodes.183506: Scattered strong to marginally severe storms were seen throughout the area from mid afternoon through the evening. Storms produced severe hail, damaging winds, and a funnel cloud across parts of eastern Iowa.
episodes.183525: Storms developed over southeast Kansas during the evening of the 13th into the morning of the 14th before moving into southwestern Missouri. These storms produced a swath of wind gusts over 60 mph from Fort Scott, Kansas to the Missouri state line and led to widespread tree and powerline damage.
episodes.183532: Storms developed over central Missouri and southeast Kansas ahead of an approaching cold front during the evening of the 12th and moved across southwest and south central Missouri through the early morning of the 13th. Sporadic wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph downed trees and power poles from Arcadia and Fort Scott in Kansas eastward to near Joplin, Billings, Marshfield, and Cabool. Widespread rainfall accumulations over an inch occurred across the entire region, with a band of two to five inches extending along and north of a line from Pittsburg, Kansas to Bolivar to Salem. Flash flooding was reported in Pittsburg, Kansas where water rescues and stranded vehicles were reported. Flash flooding also occurred near Couch in Oregon County when Townfork Creek rose rapidly out of its banks.
episodes.183533: Storms developed over eastern Oklahoma and southeast Kansas during the evening of the 13th and moved along the Missouri and Arkansas border during the early morning of the 14th. The strongest storms produced up to ping-pong ball sized hail over Oregon County. Rainfall accumulations ranged from one to two inches near the Missouri and Arkansas Border.  A second round of storms developed over central Nebraska during the morning of the 14th and moved southeastward across eastern Kansas and into the  Missouri Ozarks through the evening of the 14th. These storms produced a swath of wind gusts over 60 mph from Fort Scott, Kansas to Branson, and led to widespread tree and powerline damage. Rainfall amounts averaged between one-half inch and one inch along and west of a line from Nevada to Gainesville.
episodes.183541: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires across western Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023.
episodes.183542: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead and along a cold frontal boundary resulted in widespread downed trees and wires across southern Vermont during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13, 2023.
episodes.183597: A slow-moving cold front dropping south from the Ohio Valley. As this front encountered an airmass with modest shear and very unstable conditions, it allowed allowed for afternoon thunderstorms to develop. Some of these storms were discrete and produced large hail. After the storms began to merge into bowing segments, damaging winds resulted.
episodes.183617: Several rounds of thunderstorms moves through the area during the early morning hours on July 14th and then again into the early afternoon. These thunderstorms were forced by a stalled frontal boundary in the area with PWATs of 1.6-1.8 inches. These thunderstorms dropped anywhere from 1-3 inches of rainfall. Some locations saw upwards of 4-5 inches.
episodes.183716: Large hail and damaging winds occurred across Trego and Ellis counties.
episodes.183729: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across portions of western Nebraska early of the morning of July 14th. These storms quickly expanded in coverage as they progressed southeastward into north-central Kansas by late morning. Storms pushed through much of the eastern 2/3rds of Kansas causing widespread wind damage with recorded wind gusts up to 85 mph.
episodes.183797: A cold front moved approached New Hampshire from the west, bringing a line of showers and thunderstorms. The environment was a continuation of an anomalously moist airmass supportive of torrential rainfall. Ground conditions across New Hampshire were growing saturated, and streams were running high. The storms that developed on the evening of the 13th were concentrated across southwest New Hampshire.
episodes.183817: Another in a series of jet streaks in northwest flow aloft initiated afternoon and early evening convection across eastern South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa. Several storms in an environment of 1500-2000 MLCAPE and around 40 knots of distributed deep-layer shear took on supercellular characteristics and produced hail up to baseball size in southwest Minnesota.
episodes.183818: Another in a series of jet streaks in northwest flow aloft initiated afternoon and early evening convection across eastern South Dakota, southwest Minnesota, and northwest Iowa. Several storms in an environment of 1500-2000 MLCAPE and around 40 knots of distributed deep-layer shear took on supercellular characteristics and produced hail up to baseball size in southwest Minnesota.
episodes.183821: A couple of storms developed along a weak boundary in the late afternoon. Despite limited MLCAPE of 800-1400 J/kg and marginal deep-layer shear, a strong DCAPE up to 1000 J/kg allowed localized severe wind gusts.
episodes.183885: Thunderstorms developed into a QLCS during the afternoon of July 14th and produced widespread wind damage across the area. Winds exceeded 70 mph at times.
episodes.183956: Numerous waterspouts developed in association with developing showers along a regenerative convective cloud line flanking the Lower Florida Keys. The atmosphere consisted of high convective available energy and little if any convective inhibition.
episodes.183967: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon over the North Carolina mountains and foothills. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in McDowell County.
episodes.183969: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Chester County.
episodes.183972: A surface trough moved through, sparking a few showers and thunderstorms in northern NJ. A few thunderstorms ended up being severe, producing damaging wind gusts and hail.
episodes.183978: A few shortwaves moved through the area, with showers and thunderstorms developing in multiple rounds. Severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts in parts of New Jersey.
episodes.183980: A strong shortwave trough moved into Pennsylvania, which sparked off scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few storms became severe, producing damaging wind gusts across the eastern parts of the state.
episodes.183993: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina throughout the evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts over the Piedmont and foothills.
episodes.184003: A mesoscale convective system developed over Arkansas during the morning hours of July 14, 2023. The system fed on a very unstable and moist airmass as it moved across southwest Tennessee and north Mississippi. Isolated wind damage was reported in north Mississippi.
episodes.184017: An upper level trough and surface boundary lingered near and over the area the July 13th into July 14th. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through southeastern NY with some producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184018: An upper level trough and surface boundary lingered near and over the area the July 13th into July 14th. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through southern CT with one producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184019: An upper level trough and surface boundary lingered near and over the area the July 13th into July 14th. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through northeastern NJ with one producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184020: An upper level trough and surface boundary lingered near and over the area the July 13th into July 14th. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved over the waters with some producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184028: A thunderstorm brought 2 to 3 inches of rainfall to the northern half of Mercer County late in the evening of July 13th.  Rainfall rates at times were observed to be as much as 4 inches per hour.  Runoff from the rainfall found its way into the basement of a home, causing damage to several of the items within.
episodes.184029: Upper level low pressure was centered over Hudson Bay to start the day on the 13th, with generally zonal west to east flow from the central Plains through the Mid-Atlantic.  A slow-moving cold front was draped across the Ohio River Valley.  Early in the day, an upper level disturbance embedded in the upper level windflow was observed crossing southern Ohio and West Virginia, reaching central Virginia during the afternoon.  Thunderstorm activity increased in an environment of surface-based CAPEs climbing to around 3,000 J/Kg, while precipitable water values climbed into the 1.7 to 1.9 inch range by early evening.  A series of thunderstorms passed across the City of Lynchburg and northern Campbell County during the evening, producing 3 to locally 6 inch per hour rainfall rates.  The first storm passed across Lynchburg shortly after 4 pm, with additional rounds arriving at 6 pm, 7 pm and 9 pm.  Each round brought 1 to 3 inches of rain to the city, depending on location.  CREST Unit Streamflows rising over 1,000 cfs per mi^2.  FLASH Average Recurrence Intervals maxed out at over a 200-year rainfall event at the 6-hour duration.
episodes.184076: A mid level disturbance combined with a surface front and weak wave of low pressure moved across an unstable air mass over Vermont during the afternoon and evening of July 13th. Several lines of showers and thunderstorms moved across the region with some storms producing damaging winds, including a microburst and a weak tornado.
episodes.184098: Surface low pressure just east of the spine of the Appalachians produced heavy rains not only in North Carolina and Virginia, but also to the west of the Appalachians of northeast Tennessee, which produced flash flooding.
episodes.184129: The continuations of hail, wind, and tornadoes continues through mid-July as northwesterly upper level flow develops once again over southern Colorado. Anomalous amounts of low level moisture remain over the region due to record breaking precipitation in June and an active early July. Enhanced wind shear due from the upper level northwesterly flow created an environment conducive to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.184172: Several scattered thunderstorms developed in northwest flow and moved across the region. These storms has supercell characteristics, and were efficient hail producers. There were several reports of golfball size or larger hail.
episodes.184177: A weak boundary moved across the region and triggered a few thunderstorms. One of the stronger storms produced damaging wind in southwest Minnesota near Morton.
episodes.184287: An upper level trough and associated cold front pushed into Western New Hampshire late in the day on July 13th.  A very moist and unstable airmass was firmly in place across the state ahead of the boundary providing sufficient instability.  A line of thunderstorms pushed into the Connecticut River Valley by late evening bringing severe wind gusts and some large hail before the line weakened by the time it reached Central New Hampshire.
episodes.184329: Several scattered thunderstorms developed in northwest flow and moved across the region. These storms had supercell characteristics and were efficient hail producers. There were a couple of hail measurements between a quarter to golf-ball size hail in Barron and Dunn Counties.
episodes.184344: Isolated storms developed in an area where dewpoints in the low to mid 70s pooled. There was some weak surface convergence, ML CAPEs over 2000 J/kg, and steep low-level lapse rates, so there were some localized damaging microbursts with the severe storms. An area of storms over northern St. Clair County in Illinois produced up to 5 inches of rain in about a two hour period with some reports of flash flooding.
episodes.184376: A strong to severe cluster of storms moved through central Minnesota the evening of July 13th following the Mississippi River Valley. As the storms crossed Wabasha and Winona counties late into the overnight, a rapid intensification resulted in very large hail falling within a narrow swath of approximately 10 miles between the two counties. Hail reports varied in size from ping pong ball near Plainview (Wabasha County) to tea cup near Altura (Winona County) and Lewiston (Winona County). Significant damage was reported to crops, automobiles, and housing structures near Altura.
episodes.184381: An isolated strong storm progressed southeast following the Upper Mississippi River Valley during the evening hours of July 13th. A peak in intensity as it crossed into western Wisconsin resulted in ping pong sized hail damaging crops near Stoddard (Vernon County).
episodes.184382: Scattered strong to severe storms impacted much of the Upper Mississippi River Valley during the evening of July 14th. As storms progressed through western Wisconsin, a general weakening trend resulted in a decreased severe threat into central Wisconsin further into the evening hours. Only the first storm that persevered into central Wisconsin  was able to produce severe weather. Multiple fallen trees were reported near Greenwood and Loyal in the central part of Clark County.
episodes.184539: A very subtle surface trough axis moved generally eastward over western Lake Erie and vicinity during the evening of July 14th as a high pressure ridge exited eastward. Isolated clusters of multicell showers and thunderstorms associated with low-level convergence along the surface trough axis moved east-southeastward over western Lake Erie and northwest OH. A couple of gale-force peak convective wind gusts accompanied these cells along the northwest OH shore as the showers and storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and strong effective bulk shear.
episodes.185637: Heavy rain from slow moving thunderstorms caused flash flooding in portions of Oktibbeha county in northeastern Mississippi.

events.narrative: Trees were blown down on Belgium Hill Road.
A weather station near Lemoyne measured a 59 mph wind gust.

Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall impacted the affected area during the early evening of July 13. Radar estimates and ground observations indicated between one and a half and three inches of rain fell, leading to a few areas of flash flooding, most notably in the Castleton area along Route 30 near Lake Bomoseen.
Tree downed in the area.
Spotter reported trees blown down on power lines near Jones Rd and Centenary Rd, with other lines down in the area.
Additional thunderstorm produced more localized tree and branch damage.
A tree was downed on to power lines on Dickerson Run Road.
A tree was downed along State Route 22 north of State Route 203 near Austerlitz.
Trees were blown down on to Morgan Hill Road.
A photo was submitted, showing a large tree snapped near the trunk.
Several trees reported downed by thunderstorm winds and some siding damage to a house.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter-sized hail to the southeast of Lebanon.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down trees on Twin Rocks Road near Creamery Road.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked a tree down on Phillips Lane.
Lightning struck a tree, that then caught fire, at a private residence in the 7800 block of Red House Road in Gladys.

Shortly after midnight (EDT), a microburst occurred in a section of Framingham. There was a narrow swath of about a dozen downed trees, mainly in backyards, from Kara Ann Drive eastward across Harrington Road and onto Cynthia Road.  A few of the trees were uprooted.  One tree fell onto a car in a driveway.  A window was blown out of one garage.  This was most likely a microburst, but there is a non-zero chance that this could have been a tornado. This tornado developed on the northwest side of Mansfield, where trees were damaged. It moved southeast across the west and south sides of town. Trees were uprooted, numerous large tree limbs were snapped throughout town, poles were blown down, and homes were damaged. Trees fell onto several homes, severely damaging them. South of Mansfield, the tornado moved south-southeast uprooting a number of trees along and east of Highway 378, before dissipating on the east side of Lake Spur. Based on this damage, maximum estimated wind in the tornado was 95 to 105 mph.

A tornado touched down southeast of Applegate and tracked southeast through Townsend Road and Wixson Road. The main damage in this area was large snapped tree limbs and crop damaged. Estimated winds in this area were up to 70 mph. The beginning of the more concentrated area of damage was near the intersection of Babcock Road and Aitken Road. In this area, several large tree limbs were snapped and softwood trees uprooted in a circular pattern with one home having minor damage to fascia. Estimated peak winds in this concentrated area of damage were up to 85 mph with a width of 475 yards. The track continued moving to southeast crossing M-25 into Sanilac County Lexington Park where additional large tree limbs were downed and one snapped small softwood tree. One of the larger tree limbs fell onto a camper in the park. The track of the tornado then exited into Lake Huron.
